name: MeeTwo
oneLine: Personal agent that answers as its owner and discloses only approved information.
intuition: As I got to know more about research and engineering, I gradually realized the importance of networking. Well, it was hard for me for a while. Then it became a question of how to be polite and talk differently to different people. But I admit that talking with people, especially with experienced ones, gains valuable insights. So how could we skip the waste of time talking about useless things and find the right person we want to talk to? Let's use AI. But how? How could I know? Information exchange! Automatically. How do we avoid garbage exchange, then? How do we make sure people want to network with the AI version of me? It should know me, sound like me, but more importantly, it should be able to infer my mind, inherit my limitations as a human, and decide just like me! I am trying to make this without it telling my card number.
did: Local store of sourced, bitemporal memories, including explicit unknowns.
Default-deny airlock: only approved, versioned, reversible bundles reach the public agent.
Hybrid retrieval (keyword search and local embeddings, fused with RRF) and an eval harness that fails on any leak.

name: Table Forty Nine
oneLine: Card battler where poker hands are attacks and skill cards bend the rules.
intuition: How about turning poker into a board game? It is easy to learn as long as you know the poker rules. So no matter how weird my skill cards are, anyone who plays poker can play this, in a minute. Can you hit a royal in this game?
did: Game design and rules specification across several revisions.
Browser client and game server with real-time multiplayer.
Match-length simulation used to tune balance across table sizes.

name: Agent Relay
oneLine: Git-backed handoffs of unfinished coding tasks between collaborators' local coding agents.
intuition: My friends complain they can't use up their Codex. I was shocked. Then I invited them as my collaborators for my projects and asked them to open their computers.
did: Task state and checkpoint branches live in a shared Git remote; no hosted coordinator, database or account.
Each collaborator keeps their own machine and CLI login; finished attempts are marked for human review, never merged automatically.
Offline two-clone demo runs without a model; Claude Code and Codex adapters are experimental.

name: Agent Workspace
oneLine: Workspace for personal AI agents and tooling.
intuition: I want my Codex to talk to my Claude Code and use Gemini to organize documents and connect to my Muse to remind me and connect to Meta AI in my glasses. What? Meta AI can't connect to connectors? Send email to

name: Golfie
oneLine: Golf swing analysis from phone video: fault detection, drills, and coach review.
did: Three-phase pipeline: pose estimation, rule-based fault detection across five swing phases, LLM-generated drill plan.
Per-video pose tiers, from RTMPose on CPU to GPU models on Modal.
Coarse pass to locate the swing, then a dense pass at native frame rate to capture impact.

name: Daybook
oneLine: Local-only review of Mac Screen Time by app and purpose.
did: Imports Screen Time exports and reports hours and minutes per app.
Labels each app once as focus, entertainment or other; labels carry over to past and future days.
Local MCP interface so a personal agent can read the totals.

name: Brawl Lab
oneLine: Ranked analytics workspace and final-pick recommender for Brawl Stars.
intuition: I played Brawl Stars with my friends at college. Some of us are in different places now. But we still play. Like an escape from work, or study, or research, or relationships.... Well, we are busier now, how about saving some time by following what the data tell?
did: Calibrated logistic regression trained on about 400,000 Ranked sets.
Population map and ban guidance, counter and combo exploration, legal final-pick comparison.
Public demo on Vercel; personal data stays in a private app.

name: Dealer’s Choice
oneLine: Online multiplayer platform for home-game poker variants.
intuition: I play home games at the poker table with our friends. And I created some fun versions of my own, verified and evolved at our table for three and a half years. I want to show everyone!
did: Custom variants with real-time multiplayer over WebSocket.
ECS in private subnets behind a public ALB; CI/CD for testing and deployment.
